Rashi on Yevamot 38b:10:1.hebrew: הבן מת ראשון - ולא זכה בנכסי האב, ואין לב"ח מה לגבות:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:10:1.english: The son died first - And [therefore] he did not acquire [rights to] the father's property, and the creditor has nothing to collect.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:12:1.hebrew: יורשי האב ודאי - מוחזקים שבאין מכח ירושה ודאית, שאפי' האב מת ראשון, נכסי הבן מסתמא נופלים לפני יורשין; דאילו ב"ח מיחסר גוביינא עד שיחזיקוהו ב"ד בהם:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:12:1.english: The father's heirs [have] a definite [claim] - [They are] in possession, as they come by virtue of a definite inheritance; for even if the father died first, the son's property automatically falls to [the] heirs, whereas a creditor lacks collection until the court places him in possession of them.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:12:2.hebrew: ובעל חוב ספק - דלא הוחזק שטרו עליהן, וקאתי ספק ומוציא את החצי מידי ודאי:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:12:2.english: And the creditor [has] an uncertain [claim] - For his [debt] document has not been established against them, and [yet] an uncertain [claim] comes and extracts half from [those with] a definite [claim].

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:13:1.hebrew: כגבוי דמי - כלומר, גדול כח השטר וכמו שמוחזק בנכסים, והרי הן קמו במקום הבן ומוחזקים בנכסים דמי. הלכך, ספק וספק הוא, ואין כאן חזקה לזה יותר מזה. אם האב מת ראשון, הוחזק ב"ח מיד, ולא אמרינן הא מחוסר גוביינא; ואם בן מת ראשון, הוחזקו יורשים:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:13:1.english: [It] is as though [it were] collected - That is to say, the power of the bill [of debt] is great, and [it is] as though [the creditor] is in possession of the property, and behold, they stand in the place of the son and are considered to be in possession of the property. Therefore, it is [a case of] equal uncertainty, and neither has a stronger presumption [of possession] here than the other. If the father died first, the creditor immediately came into possession, and we do not say, "Behold, it still lacks collection"; and if [the] son died first, the [father's] heirs came into possession.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:14:1.hebrew: מתו בעליהן - כל אשה שקנא לה בעלה ונסתרה ומת עד שלא שתתה, נוטלת כתובתה, ואע"פ ששמא זינתה ואין לה כתובה:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:14:1.english: Their husbands died - Any woman whose husband warned her [not to seclude herself] and she secluded herself, and [he] died before she drank [the bitter waters], collects her marriage contract, even though perhaps she committed adultery and has no [right to a] marriage contract.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:14:2.hebrew: לא שותות - דבעינן "והביא האיש את אשתו", וליכא:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:14:2.english: [They] do not drink - For we require, "and the man shall bring his wife" [Numbers 5:15], and [that is] lacking.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:16:1.hebrew: מידי ודאי - מידי יורשי הבעל שהן מוחזקין ודאי, מוציאה זו כתובה מספק:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:16:1.english: From the hands of a definite [possessor] - From the hands of the husband's heirs, who are definitely in possession, this [woman] extracts [her] ketubah on an uncertain [claim].

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:16:2.hebrew: אלא - לאו ש"מ קסברי ב"ש שטר העומד לגבות כגבוי דמי, וכיון שמת עמדו הנכסים מיד בחזקת האשה, ויורשים קאתו לאפוקי מינה משום ספק זנאי, ולא אתי ספק ומוציא מידי ודאי? דאי לא כגבוי דמי, וטעמא משום דאתי ספק ומוציא מידי ודאי הוא, הוה להו למימר יחלוקו, ונשווי ספק כודאי, אבל לעלויי מינה ליכא למ"ד. וגבי נפל הבית קאמר יחלוקו, דכי נמי אמרי' כגבוי דמי, לא מצינו לב"ח לשוויי ודאי טפי מיורשין, שהרי לא הוחזק בו זה בנכסים, והשטר זה יוצא עליו ולא על האב. הלכך ספק וספק הוא: אם האב מת ראשון, נמצא ב"ח ודאי — דהאי שטר כגבוי דמי — ויורשים אינם כלום; ואם הבן מת ראשון, נמצאו יורשין ודאין וב"ח אין כלום:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:16:2.english: Rather - Does it not follow from this that Beit Shammai hold [that] a bill [of debt] awaiting collection is [considered] as already collected, and once [her husband] died, the property immediately stood in the presumptive possession of the wife, and the heirs are coming to extract [it] from her on account of an uncertainty [whether] she was unfaithful, and an uncertain [claim] cannot come and extract [property] from a definite [claim]? For if it were not [considered] as already collected, and the reason were that an uncertain [claim] comes and extracts from a definite [claim], they should have said 'they divide,' and we would treat an uncertain [claim] like a definite [claim]; but to elevate [an uncertain claim] above [a definite one], there is no one who holds that. And regarding [the case where] 'the house collapsed,' [the Mishnah] says 'they divide,' because even when we say [it is] as already collected, we cannot make the creditor more of a definite [claimant] than the heirs, since this [creditor] was not established in possession of the property, and this bill [of debt] is issued against him [the son] and not against the father. Therefore, it is [a case of] uncertain versus uncertain: if the father died first, the creditor is a definite [claimant] — since this bill is [considered] as already collected — and the heirs have nothing; and if the son died first, the heirs are definite [claimants] and the creditor has nothing:

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:17:1.hebrew: ואביי - דלא אסיק אדעתיה מעיקרא משום טעמא דשטר העומד לגבות, כי אותביה לרבה מנפל הבית, דתנן במי שמת בבבא בתרא בסדר ישועות:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:17:1.english: And Abaye - who did not initially think [of it] because of the reason of a document that stands to be collected, when he objected to Rabbah from [the case of] "the house fell," which we learned in the Mishnah in [the chapter] Mi SheMeit in Bava Batra, in Seder Yeshu'ot [Nezikin].

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:17:2.hebrew: לותביה מהא - דמתני' היא בסדר נשים, דהכא נמי ספק מוציא מידי ודאי:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:17:2.english: Let him object to him from this - For it is a Mishnah in Seder Nashim, where here too an uncertain [claim] extracts [property] from a definite [claim].

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:17:3.hebrew: ואביי - להכי לא אותביה מכתובה, דקסבר שאני כתובה משום חינא, שיהיו נושאין חן בעיני הנשים ויתרצו להנשא; לפיכך החזיקוה מספק:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:17:3.english: And Abaye - This is why he did not raise an objection against him from [the case of] a marriage contract: because he holds [that] a marriage contract is different on account of desirability, so that [men] will find favor in the eyes of women and they will consent to marry; therefore, [the Sages] granted her possession [of it] despite the doubt.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:18:1.hebrew: ולותביה מכתובה דמתני' - דאמרי ב"ש יחלוקו, דקס"ד השתא דב"ש נמי אכתובה אמרי יחלוקו, וקאתו יורשין דידה מספק וגבו פלגא דכתובה מיבם דהוי ודאי. והתם ליכא למימר משום חינא, דהתם מתה, וגבי יורשין לא חיישינן לחינא, כדאמר באלמנה ניזונת (כתובות צז:), אא"כ היו יורשיה נקבות:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:18:1.english: And let him object to him from the ketubah of our Mishnah - Where Beit Shammai say "they shall divide," for we currently assume that Beit Shammai also say "they shall divide" regarding the ketubah, and her heirs come with an uncertain [claim] and collect half of the ketubah from the yavam, who is in certain [possession]. And there one cannot say [it is] because of [finding] favor, for there she died, and regarding heirs we are not concerned about [finding] favor, as it says in [the chapter] Almanah Nizonet (Ketubot 97b), unless her heirs were females.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:19:1.hebrew: לא פליגי - דמודו ב"ש שהיא בחזקת יורשי הבעל, דלא ניתנה כתובה לגבות מחיים, וכל שהיא מתה בחייו של יבם לא גבו יורשים דילה כתובה, דיבם במקום בעל קאי. ואע"ג דשמעינן ליה לאביי בכתובות פרק האשה (דף פא.) ניתנה כתובה לגבות מחיים לב"ש, הני מילי להתחייב יבם בקבורתה, דאמר מינה קא ירית כתובה ולא מאחיו, אבל דלישקלו יורשין דילה כתובתה, לא שמעינן ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:19:1.english: They do not disagree - for Beit Shammai concede that it [the marriage contract] is in the presumptive possession of the husband's heirs, since a marriage contract is not given to be collected during [the husband's] lifetime, and whenever she dies during the lifetime of the yavam, her heirs do not collect [her] marriage contract, because a yavam stands in the place of the husband. And even though we heard Abaye [state] in Ketubot, chapter HaIsha (81a), [that] a marriage contract is given to be collected during [the husband's] lifetime according to Beit Shammai, that applies [only] to obligating the yavam for her burial, for he says [that] he inherits [her] marriage contract from her and not from his brother; but that her heirs should take her marriage contract, we have not heard him [say].

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:1:1.hebrew: סיפא - דגבי נשואה בעלמא אמרי' לקמן דברי הכל מכרה ונתנה, אפי' בדיעבד הבעל מוציא מיד הלקוחות; הכא לגבי זיקת נשואה, דספק היא ולא כנשואה ממש, קיימי נכסי בספק. הלכך, לב"ש חלוקה עדיפא [ולב"ה חזקה עדיפא]:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:1:1.english: The latter clause - For regarding an ordinary married woman, we say later on [that] everyone agrees [that if] she sold or gave [away her property], even after the fact the husband recovers [it] from the buyers; here, regarding a levirate bond of a married woman — which is an uncertainty and not like an actual married woman — the property stands in doubt. Therefore, according to Beit Shammai, division is preferable [and according to Beit Hillel, possession is preferable].

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:21:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי כו' - וטעמא לא משום דשטר העומד לגבות הוא, דלא ניתנה כתובה לגבות מחיים:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:21:1.english: [The mishna] is also precise, etc. - And the reason is not because [a marriage contract] is a document that stands to be collected, for a marriage contract is not given to be collected during [the husband's] lifetime.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:21:2.english: The husband's heirs with the father's heirs - [Referring to] melog [usufruct] property.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:22:1.hebrew: אביי - מהדר ארישא דשמעתין לתרוצי: מאי שנא רישא דלא פליגי, ומאי שנא סיפא דפליגי? ותרציה: לאו משום דברישא היא קיימת וסיפא משום דליתא, דודאי סיפא נמי, אי כשהיא שומרת יבם נפלו לה, מודו ב"ש דיורשי האב ודאין ונכסים בחזקתן. אלא רישא דנפלו לה כשהיא שומרת יבם, לפיכך מוכרת לכתחלה; וה"ה אם מתה, יורשיה יורשין אותה, דלא מהניא זיקה למיקני נכסי דהשתא:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:22:1.english: Abaye - [He] goes back to the beginning of our passage to resolve [the question]: What is the difference [between] the first clause, where they do not disagree, and the latter clause, where they do disagree? And he resolved it: [It is] not because in the first clause she is alive and [in] the latter clause because she is not [alive], for certainly [in] the latter clause too, if [the properties] fell to her when she was awaiting a yavam, Beit Shammai agree that the father's heirs are definite [heirs] and the properties [remain] in their possession. Rather, the first clause [is a case] where [the properties] fell to her when she was awaiting a yavam; therefore she may sell [them] from the outset; and the same applies if she dies — her heirs inherit her, because the levirate bond is not effective to acquire properties [that came to her] now.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:22:2.english: The latter clause, where [property] fell to her when she was - under her first husband.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:2:1.hebrew: זיקת ארוסה - זיקת יבמה שנפלה מן האירוסין, ספק ארוסה ולא ודאי ארוסה. ואע"ג דלגבי נכסים אין לו שום כח בהן, ונמצא שזיקת ארוסה אינה כלום, קרי לה ספק ארוסה, דלא מצי למימר קסבר עולא זיקת ארוסה אינה כלום, דהא בעיא חליצה:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:2:1.english: A levirate bond with a betrothed woman - [This refers to] the levirate bond of a yevamah who fell [to the levir] from betrothal — [it renders her] a woman of uncertain betrothal, and not a woman of definite betrothal. And even though with respect to [her] property he has no authority over it at all, and it thus turns out that a levirate bond with a betrothed woman is nothing [in that regard], [the Gemara] calls her "a woman of uncertain betrothal" because it cannot say [that] Ulla holds a levirate bond with a betrothed woman is nothing [altogether], since she requires chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:2:2.hebrew: מודים ב"ה כו' - בתמיה. אלא ש"מ כספק ארוסה היא, הלכך תמכור לכתחלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:2:2.english: Would Beit Hillel concede, etc. - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question. Rather, learn from this [that] she is like a woman of uncertain betrothal; therefore, she may sell [her property] ab initio.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:5:1.hebrew: עושה ספק נשואה - כדפרישית לעיל, דכיון דודאי נשואה הבעל מוציא מיד הלקוחות, הכא דספק נשואה היא — הוו נכסים בספק. ולב"ש חלוקה עדיפא, דאין לה בהם חזקה יותר ממנו, דידו כידה; ולב"ה חזקה עדיפא, דאין ידו כידה, הואיל ולא נפלו לה כשהיא תחת הבעל:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:5:1.english: Makes [her] a doubtfully married woman - As I explained above, since [in the case of] a definitely married woman the husband repossesses [the property] from the purchasers, here, where she is a doubtfully married woman, the property is [in a state of] uncertainty. According to Beit Shammai, division is preferable, for she does not have a stronger claim of possession over [the property] than he does, since his hand [i.e., his right] is equal to hers; and according to Beit Hillel, [her] possession is preferable, for his hand is not equal to hers, since [the property] did not fall to her [as an inheritance] while she was under the husband['s authority].

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:6:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רבה - לעולא. אי טעמא משום חלוקה עדיפא הוא, אדמיפלגי בגופה של קרקע ולאחר מיתה, ליפלגו בחייה ולפירות! דלב"ש פליג יבם פירי בהדה, דספק נשואה היא — דאילו ודאי נשואה הואי, הוה שקיל להו בעל כרחה — ולב"ה נכסים בחזקתה ולא שקיל מידי. ומדנקט מתני' מיתה בסיפא, ש"מ טעמייהו דב"ש ברישא, דאלמוה לחזקה דילה משום דהיא קיימא:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:6:1.english: Rabba said to him - to Ulla: If the reason [for Beit Shammai's ruling] is that division is preferable, instead of disagreeing about the principal of the land and after [her] death, let them disagree during her lifetime and about the produce! For according to Beit Shammai, the yavam divides the produce with her, since she is possibly married [to him] — for if she were definitely married [to him], he would take it against her will — whereas according to Beit Hillel, the property [remains] in her presumptive possession and he takes nothing. And from the fact that the Mishnah specifies death in the latter clause, learn from this that Beit Shammai's reason in the first clause is that they strengthened her presumptive possession because she is alive.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:7:1.english: Rather, Rabbah said: Both this and that [are] where she fell - for levirate marriage when she was a married woman, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:7:2.hebrew: איהי ודאי - שהקרן שלה ממה נפשך, הלכך אלימא חזקה דילה:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:7:2.english: She [has] a definite [claim] - For the principal is hers either way; therefore, her presumptive possession is stronger.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:8:1.hebrew: סיפא - הואיל ומתה, הללו באים וטוענים מכח ירושה והיבם טוען מכח ירושה. הלכך, שניהם ספק לב"ש, דאי זיקה ככנוסה אין כאן ליורשי האב כלום, שהבעל יורש שלה, ואי לאו ככנוסה אין כאן ליבם כלום; לפיכך ספק וספק הוא ויחלוקו. ולב"ה, הואיל ואלו קרובין ודאין הם והוחזקה נחלה זו כבר בחזקת משפחתן, אמרינן אוקי אחזקתה. אבל בחייה ולפירות, אפי' ב"ש מודו דנכסים בחזקתייהו ולא שקיל בעל מידי:
Rashi on Yevamot 38b:8:1.english: The latter clause - Since she died, these [heirs of the father] come and claim by right of inheritance, and the yavam claims by right of inheritance. Therefore, both [claims] are uncertain according to Beit Shammai: for if [the levirate] bond [is considered] like a consummated marriage, the father's heirs have nothing here, since the husband inherits from her; and if [it is] not like a consummated marriage, the yavam has nothing here. Accordingly, it is [a case of equal] uncertainty on both sides, and they divide [the property]. And according to Beit Hillel, since these [heirs of the father] are definite relatives and this inheritance has already been established in the presumptive possession of their family, we say: Leave it in its presumptive possession. However, during her lifetime and regarding the produce, even Beit Shammai agree that the property remains in their presumptive possession and the husband takes nothing.

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:9:1.english: Upon him and upon his heirs - We do not read [this].

Rashi on Yevamot 38b:9:2.english: A house collapsed, etc. - He has no property, while those from whom he inherits have property.

Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:13:1.hebrew: קסברי ב"ש שטר העומד לגבות כגבוי דמי - אביי גופיה אית ליה הכי בפרק האשה שנפלו (כתובות דף פא. ושם), דלבתר דשמע מרבה סברה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:13:1.english: Beit Shammai hold [that] a bill [of debt] awaiting collection is [considered] as though collected - Abaye himself holds this [view] in the chapter [entitled] HaIshah SheNaflu (Ketubot 81a and there), for after he heard [it] from Rabbah, he accepted it.

Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:14:1.hebrew: בש"א נוטלות כתובה ולא שותות - והא דתנן בריש פ' ארוסה (סוטה דף כג:): "ארוסה ושומרת יבם לא שותות ולא נוטלות כתובתן", ולא פליגי ב"ש — אור"י, דהתם היא נתנה אצבע בין שיניה, שנסתרה ואסרה עצמה על בעלה; אבל הכא, בשעה שנסתרה היתה יכולה ליבדק בשתיה. ועוד, דבארוסה ושומרת יבם אין לחושבה כעוברת על דת, כיון שאינה יכולה ליבדק, כדקאמר התם בגמ':
Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:14:1.english: Beit Shammai say: They collect their marriage contract and do not drink - And [as for] that which we learned in the Mishnah at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Arusah (Sotah 23b): "A betrothed woman and a woman awaiting a levir neither drink nor collect their marriage contract," and Beit Shammai do not disagree [there] — Rabbi Yitzchak says that there, she put her finger between her teeth [i.e., she brought it upon herself], since she secluded herself and [thereby] forbade herself to her husband; whereas here, at the time she secluded herself, she was able to be tested through drinking [the bitter waters]. And furthermore, in [the case of] a betrothed woman and a woman awaiting a levir, she is not to be considered as one who transgresses the law, since she cannot be tested, as it says there in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:14:2.hebrew: בה"א או שותות או לא נוטלות כו' - הא דגרס במסכת סוטה (דף כד.): "לא שותות ולא נוטלות כתובה", כתבו שם כמו שמגיה הש"ס כאן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:14:2.english: Beit Hillel say: "Either they drink or they do not collect, etc." - That which [the text] reads in Tractate Sotah (24a): "they neither drink nor collect [their] marriage contract," they wrote there as the Talmud emends [it] here.

Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:17:1.hebrew: ואביי לותביה מהא - וא"ת: אדרבה, תקשי ליה למה נוטלת כל הכתובה מספק? וי"ל: לפי שהיא באה בטענת ברי, והיורשין בטענת ספק:
Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:17:1.english: And Abaye, let him object to him from this! - And if you ask: On the contrary, it should be a difficulty for him why she collects the entire marriage contract [in a case of] doubt? One can answer: Because she comes with a claim of certainty, whereas the heirs [come] with a claim of doubt:

Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:1:1.hebrew: זיקת נשואה עושה ספק נשואה - ואפ"ה לב"ה הוו בחזקת יורשי האב, דחזקה עדיפא, שיש לנו להחזיק נחלה בחזקת אותו השבט:
Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:1:1.english: A levirate bond [with] a married woman renders [her] a doubtfully married woman - And even so, according to Beit Hillel, [the properties] remain in the presumptive possession of the father's heirs, because a presumptive status [chazakah] is stronger, as we must maintain an inheritance in the presumptive possession of that tribe.

Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:4:1.hebrew: דאי ס"ד ודאי נשואה והתנן נפלו לה כו' - מכמה משניות דתנן פרק יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קח.) שהבעל יורש את אשתו, הוה מצי למיפרך; אלא מסיפא דההוא דאייתי לעיל נ"ל לאיתויי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:4:1.english: "Because if it enters your mind [that her status is that of] a definitely married woman... and didn't we learn [in a Mishnah]: If [property] fell to her, etc." - It could have raised an objection from several Mishnayot that we learned in Chapter Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 108a) [teaching] that a husband inherits his wife; rather, it was preferable for [the Gemara] to cite from the latter clause of that [Mishnah] that it cited above.

Tosafot on Yevamot 38b:7:1.english: She has a certain [claim] - because the principal [of the property] is hers:
